title: Rabbi Nechemyah (Disputed Transmission)
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He spoke in Rabbi Nechemyah’s name, according to Seder HaDorot’s citation of Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 1:2.

With respect, that work did not examine the Jerusalem Talmud. It reads: “The Mishnah of Rabbi is only according to Rabbi Nechemyah, in Rabbi Nechemyah’s name: the Aramaic gourd is the Egyptian gourd.” A small error has entered the text. Its clear meaning is that Rabbi’s Mishnah—which says that Egyptian and ramutza gourds are not prohibited mixtures—is not according to Rabbi Nechemyah, who says in Tosefta Kilayim, chapter 1, that they are prohibited mixtures with each other.

notes.text: Hyman’s point is that a small error created the appearance of Nechemyah speaking in Nechemyah’s name. His proposed reading restores the negation “not according to.” The checked text has that negation.

The inspected Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 1:2 already has the negation not according to Rabbi Nechemyah. Hyman’s diagnosis of a small error creating a Nechemyah-in-Nechemyah’s-name chain remains his textual argument.
